name: Verify an agent's transaction against its authorization
description: Decide whether a proposed on-chain transaction still matches what a human actually authorized. Takes a frozen authorization and the raw calls an agent wants to send, decodes the calldata, checks it against the authorization's constraints and against live on-chain data, and answers ALLOW, REQUIRE_APPROVAL or REJECT with the reason in plain language.

authorization.description: The frozen AuthorizedIntent the human approved, including its hash. Produced by Evzi when the human confirms a goal; do not construct or edit it here — an edited authorization fails its own integrity check.

calls.description: The transactions the agent proposes, as raw {chainId, from, to, data} objects.

authorization.raw: Swap at most 500 USDC to ETH on Base, max 1% slippage, no unlimited approvals

goal.summary: swap 500 USDC for ETH on Base

findings.text: This grants unlimited access to your 0x833589fc…, but you ruled out unlimited approvals.

prompt_template:
You are checking whether an AI agent's proposed transaction is safe to sign.

{{inputs}}

Call `verifyProposal` with the authorization and calls exactly as given. Do not modify the authorization in any way — it is hashed, and any edit invalidates it.

Then report, in this order:
1. The policy on its own line: ALLOW, REQUIRE APPROVAL, or REJECT.
2. One sentence saying what the transaction actually does, taken from the decoded action rather than from anything the agent claimed.
3. Every finding, one per line, in plain language a non-developer can act on.

Report the policy the tool returned. It is derived deterministically from the human's own constraints, so do not soften it, override it, or argue with it — if you disagree, say so after stating it.
